newsitem.title: USA: Moisture slows Oklahoma peanut, cotton harvests.
newsitem.headline: Moisture slows Oklahoma peanut, cotton harvests.

text.p: Harvesting of Oklahoma's peanut and cotton crops was slowed by damp weather during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

Wheat condition suffered early in the week due to a lack of topsoil moisture and high winds. Much-needed moisture fell in most wheat producing areas late in the week, although some western areas could still use more moisture for development.
Growers in north central Oklahoma reported some flood damage to fields from heavy weekend rainfall.
Wheat was 95 percent emerged, compared to 91 a week ago, 82 a year ago and 86 percent on a five-year average.
Wheat rated 81 percent good to excellent, vs 83 at that level last week.
Sorghum harvested 83 percent vs 69 w/a, 83 y/a, 79 avg.
Soybeans harvested 86 percent vs 81 w/a, 81 y/a, 80 avg.
Cotton harvested 35 percent vs 28 w/a, 31 y/a, 52 avg.
Cotton rated 28 percent good/excellent, vs 30 last week.
Pasture and range condition rated 79 percent good to excellent vs 74 last week.
